name: Octisalate

lead: Octisalate is a salicylate-based sunscreen ingredient that absorbs a little UVB light. Its main job is to raise SPF and help keep filters like avobenzone from breaking down, so a daily sunscreen protects skin from photoaging.

It is also an emollient that adds water resistance to formulas. It is a minor filter with less research than headline ingredients, mostly absorption and allergy studies. A 2020 JAMA trial found it enters the bloodstream.

paras: It is part of daily sunscreens and SPF moisturisers, where it is blended with other filters rather than used alone.

Wikipedia says under 1% penetrates the skin and sensitisation potential is minor. European regulators required endocrine-related testing in 2020, and it is classed as highly toxic to aquatic life in REACH registrations.

angle.text: Octisalate boosts SPF and steadies other filters, so daily sunscreen limits UV damage and slows visible skin aging. The evidence is for sunscreen formulas as a class.

lead: Octisalate (octyl salicylate, 2-ethylhexyl salicylate) is an ester of salicylic acid used in sunscreens and cosmetics as a weak UVB absorber, usually added to boost SPF and to help stabilise other filters such as avobenzone and oxybenzone [1]. It is also an emollient that adds water resistance [1].

It is one of the six active ingredients assessed in 2020 JAMA trial of sunscreen absorption, which found that all were absorbed into the bloodstream [2]. Regulators in Europe have required additional endocrine-related testing, which a company contested unsuccessfully in court [1].

paras: Octisalate is called a weak UVB absorber, though it is more stable than some alternatives, and is used to improve the performance of filters such as oxybenzone and avobenzone and to reduce their photodegradation [1]. US labels list it in SPF foundations paired with titanium dioxide and in moisturisers paired with other filters, with standard warnings to stop use if a rash occurs [3]. A photostability study compared combinations of UV filters in a sunscreen [4].

Wikipedia cites a 2007 review finding a good safety profile for salicylates, no reactive oxygen species formation in sunlight, and minor sensitisation potential [1]. Company REACH registrations classify it as highly toxic to aquatic life and suspected of causing fetal harm, and in 2020 the European Chemicals Agency required a fish sexual-development test because of possible endocrine activity [1]. Octyl salicylate and other filters have been measured in human placental tissue and tested for in vitro endocrine activity [5], and in river and lake water in Japan [6]; reviews address endocrine disruption potential in aquatic environments [7].

Human data are limited to absorption and allergy. The 2020 JAMA randomised trial measured plasma levels of octisalate among six ingredients [2], a phase 1 registration enrolled 72 participants [8], and a 1,000-participant European photopatch study examined photoallergy to sunscreen ingredients [9]. A 1995 study found that a high-SPF sunscreen prevented UVB-induced immunosuppression in humans, but it tested a sunscreen as a whole [10].

timeline.event: JAMA trial reports plasma absorption of octisalate and five other sunscreen ingredients; ECHA requires a fish endocrine test [2][1].
